bib.title: AgentArk: Distilling Multi-Agent Intelligence into a Single LLM Agent

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AgentArk: Distilling Multi-Agent Intelligence into a Single LLM Agent", Yinyi Luo (CMU, first author) with Jin, Yu, Zhang, Kumar, Li, Xu, Chen, Wang (CMU, W&M, GaTech, Amazon, UBC). arXiv:2602.03955v3 [cs.AI], 23 May 2026 (v1 Feb 2026). No venue printed: preprint. Code: github.com/AIFrontierLab/AgentArk.
COVERAGE: all 32 of 32 pages, 87,388 chars, including appendices A-I and Tables 3-13. Figures are only partly readable from text (bar charts, no numbers). References skimmed.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Headline: distilling 5-agent debate into one model lifts a single agent by about 4.8% on average and lands only slightly below the vanilla multi-agent debate. The paper gives no table for this average; it points to a figure and Appendix G.2.
  number: 4.8%
  setup: teacher Qwen3-32B, students Qwen3-8B, 1.7B, 0.6B, Llama3-8B-Instruct, Gemma-7B; 5 debating agents, 120 experiments in total; accuracy on GSM8K, MATH, MedMCQA, MetaMathQA.
  quote: "AgentArk significantly improves the performance of a single agent by 4.8% and only slightly worse than the vanilla MAS."
  where: p.6
- In-domain gains are far larger than out-of-domain gains.
  number: 30% vs 7% max; 4-6% vs 1-3% average
  setup: Qwen3-32B teacher; the max figures are the best cells, probably the DA/RSFT rows on MetaMathQA.
  quote: "the gain in ID is more significant than in the OOD setting (30% vs. 7% maximum improvement and 4-6% vs. 1-3% on average)"
  where: p.6
- PAD is the most consistent method; RSFT and DA are inconsistent. The appendix tables show PAD gains are tiny on Qwen3-8B and often under 1 point. DA and RSFT swing widely: DA on Qwen3-0.6B trained on MetaMathQA and tested on GSM8K reaches 53.37 from 41.93, while RSFT drops to 21-39 in some cells.
  number: PAD Qwen3-8B 88.17 base -> 89.05 / 89.02 / 89.15 / 88.7 (32B teacher, trained on GSM8K, MedMCQA, MetaMathQA and MATH, tested on GSM8K); one PAD cell on MedMCQA 59.65 -> 63.12
  setup: Tables 9-13, p.27-31. Each cell appears to be a single run. No seeds or confidence intervals are reported.
  quote: "While RSFT and DA sometimes provide improvements, their gains are inconsistent and can fluctuate by dataset. In contrast, PAD consistently yields performance improvements"
  where: p.6
- Answer-only SFT (the plain SFT baseline) does not help on GSM8K and often hurts. This is the closest thing to an "SFT vs distillation" ablation.
  number: Qwen3-8B trained on GSM8K gets 81.35 on GSM8K against a base of 88.17; Qwen3-0.6B gets 37.91 against 41.93; Llama3-8B gets 63.61 against 75.28. Gemma-7B on GSM8K rises to 56.56 from 51.1. On MedMCQA, answer-only SFT gives +6.8 (Gemma-7B) and +3.4 (Qwen3-8B).
  setup: Table 8, Appendix G.1, p.25-26. Ground-truth input-output pairs only.
  quote: "Even when trained directly on GSM8K, models frequently underperform their base counterparts."
  where: p.25
- Reasoning-quality analysis. PAD scores highest on LLM-judge reasoning coherence and intermediate verification. RSFT and DA get lower perplexity and NLL than PAD.
  number: Reasoning Coherence 1.88 (single) / 2.25 (RSFT) / 3.07 (DA) / 3.96 (PAD); Intermediate Verification 2.41 / 3.48 / 4.04 / 4.07; perplexity 1.9211 / 1.6388 / 1.5603 / 1.7996
  setup: Qwen3-32B teacher, Qwen3-0.6B student, held-out GSM8K, 100 samples, judge InternLM-2.5-20b-chat. In the text, "PAD achieves the highest scores in all metrics" is not accurate for step decomposition (DA 3.38 vs PAD 3.23), intermediate verification (DA 4.04 vs PAD 4.07, roughly tied), or error localization (DA 2.91 vs PAD 2.78).
  quote: "Reasoning Coherence (↑) 1.88 2.25 3.07 3.96"
  where: p.9 (Table 1a)
- PRM capacity matters more than student size in the paper's ablation, but the effect is tiny. Policy size dominates absolute accuracy. PRM 0.6B vs 8B with an 8B policy moves GSM8K only 88.52 -> 88.59 average (MedMCQA 59.66 -> 59.80); with a 0.6B policy there is no gain (42.63 vs 42.63).
  number: 88.52 vs 88.59
  setup: Table 4, p.20. Distilled from Qwen3-32B, GSM8K and MedMCQA test sets.
  quote: "effective distillation relies more critically on the modeling size of the PRM than on the scale of the policy itself"
  where: p.20
- More debate agents or more data does not help small students. For 0.6B, more than 5 agents gives no gain and sometimes hurts. For 8B, gains are modest and diminishing. RSFT and DA vary non-monotonically with data size; PAD is more stable.
  number: agents 5/10/20; data 10 to 7,473 (GSM8K) and 15 to 150,000 (MetaMathQA)
  setup: Qwen3-32B teacher; Fig.3 and Fig.4 (p.7). Values are read from charts only.
  quote: "for capacity-limited students, reasoning quality rather than data volume is the primary bottleneck."
  where: p.8
- Comparison with on-policy self-distillation. The ordering in the text is garbled.
  number: "+0.99% vs. +1.62%" on GSM8K
  setup: no model, size or settings stated in the section.
  quote: "Our PAD method outperforms SD (+0.99% vs. +1.62% on GSM8K)."
  where: p.8. The quoted numbers read as if SD gained more than PAD. Treat as unreliable and do not cite the ordering.
- Training cost against inference cost. The paper gives no inference-cost numbers: no latency, tokens or GPU-hours for debate vs the distilled student. It only says single generation is cheaper.
  number: RSFT about 6 h on 1xH100; DA about 8 h on 1xH100; PAD about 20 h on 8xH100 (PRM about 8 h plus GRPO about 12 h)
  setup: 8B student, global batch size 4; debate data generation cost excluded (shared by all methods).
  quote: "PAD (PRM + GRPO) PRM training + GRPO-based policy optimization 8×H100∼20 hours"
  where: p.23 (Table 6)
- Other MAS protocols (AgentVerse, Self-Consistency): gains over single agent are tiny, about 0.1-0.4 points. Heterogeneous teachers (five different model families): Qwen3-1.7B 69.14 -> 69.69 under PAD; Gemma-7B 51.10 -> 53.21 under PAD and 53.77 under DA.
  number: Qwen3-8B GSM8K 88.17 -> 88.53 (AgentVerse, PAD) and 88.58 (Self-Consistency, PAD)
  setup: Table 2, p.10. Qwen3-32B to Qwen3-8B, trained on GSM8K, no seeds.
  quote: "AgentVerse 88.17 / 59.65 88.12 / 59.70 88.48 / 59.85 88.53 / 59.78"
  where: p.10
- Out-of-domain open-ended: trained on GSM8K only, tested on HotpotQA, QASPER and QMSum. Gains are small and larger for 8B. Qwen3-8B on QMSum F1 14.94 -> 17.82; the 0.6B student shows little benefit.
  number: 14.94 -> 17.82
  setup: Appendix D.1, p.21. Which distillation method produced "Ours" is not stated.
  quote: "Qwen3-8B improves its F1-Score from 14.94 to 17.82 and its ROUGE-L Score from 15.72 to 17.41."
  where: p.21
- Stacking DA on RSFT or PAD gives modest gains of about 0.5-1.7 points. Qwen3-1.7B, Table 7, p.25.
- PPO vs GRPO: comparable (53.10 vs 52.61 GSM8K average); GRPO is cheaper. Table 5, p.21. Table 5 is for the Gemma-7B student.
- Data pipeline: 5 debaters plus a summarizer, up to K=3 rounds; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct filters for correctness and judges diversity; about 342k questions and 2M trajectories in total (p.18). Problems with fewer than 2 correct agents are dropped from DA.
- TruthfulQA "robustness": BLEU 0.6034 (single) -> 0.6634 (PAD), 0.6353 (DA), 0.6059 (RSFT). Qwen3-8B, p.9. This is a similarity metric, which is a weak robustness measure.

LIMITS
- Authors concede (p.10) that experiments cover only a subset of reasoning benchmarks and multimodal models, and use one specific set of distillation pipelines. Tool use and memory are out of scope (footnote, p.2). The main setting is homogeneous agents.
- Not shown: the multi-agent debate baseline numbers are not tabulated in the extracted text, so "slightly worse than MAS" cannot be checked. There is no inference latency or cost table. There are no seeds, variances or significance tests. There is no direct SFT vs PAD matched-data ablation beyond the answer-only SFT of Table 8, which differs in data from RSFT. There is no check against stronger or simpler baselines such as rejection-sampling SFT or plain RL from verifiable reward.
- Most Qwen3-8B gains are under 1 point and look like noise. Qwen3-8B base GSM8K is already 88.17. The headline 4.8% is dominated by the weak students (Gemma-7B, Qwen3-0.6B) and by the MetaMathQA-trained rows.
- PRM labels come from consensus with the debate and from answer correctness, so the PRM may reinforce majority errors. The authors warn distilled students may inherit flawed reasoning (p.32).
- Text and table inconsistencies. The "Table X" reference in B.2. The PPO claim "marginally higher" is described as GRPO "comparable". The 0.6B student's gains in the data-scaling Fig.4 are reported only as accuracy of 40-50. Fig.9 is labelled MedMCQA but its y-axis says GSM8K.
- The paper cites the AI-written-assistance use (Appendix H).

BUILDS ON: Du et al. 2023 (multiagent debate); Liang et al. 2024 (divergent-thinking debate, 5 agents); Lightman et al. 2023 and Wang et al. 2024 Math-Shepherd (PRMs); Shao et al. 2024 DeepSeekMath (GRPO); Schulman et al. 2017 (PPO); MAGDi (Chen et al. 2024), Chain-of-Agents (Li et al. 2025), Kim et al. 2025 "Towards a science of scaling agent systems" (claims MAS structure matters less than reasoning dynamics); Wang et al. 2022 self-consistency; Chen et al. 2023 AgentVerse; Zhao-type on-policy self-distillation [71].

CODE: none. Key equations: PRM contrastive loss, Eq.6 (p.19); GRPO advantage from PRM score Â_i=(R_φ(o_i)-μ_R)/σ_R (p.5).

FIGURES (not extracted via captions script; read from text)
- Fig.1 p.3: pipeline overview, debate -> extraction -> RSFT/DA/PAD (PRM + GRPO).
- Fig.2 p.6: improvement of each method per student, in-domain vs OOD.
- Fig.3 p.7: agent-count scaling. Fig.4 p.7: data-size scaling.
- Table 1 p.9 and Table 6 p.23 are the most useful tables.

PROBLEMS: Text extraction is clean enough. The charts have no numeric labels. Garbled text about SD numbers (p.8). No embedded instructions found. Cost and baseline-debate numbers are not in the extracted text, so I left them out rather than guess.

Suggested verbatim quotes with page numbers: (1) p.6 "AgentArk significantly improves the performance of a single agent by 4.8% and only slightly worse than the vanilla MAS." (2) p.25 "Even when trained directly on GSM8K, models frequently underperform their base counterparts." (3) p.8 "for capacity-limited students, reasoning quality rather than data volume is the primary bottleneck."
